items.body:
China pushed back against the United States in its speech at the UN General Assembly on Saturday, saying sovereignty of countries in the Gulf should be respected and urging the "relevant country" to stop threatening Cuba and lift its blockade on it.
Vice President Han Zheng did not mention the US by name in his remarks. The US has [USN:S0N44A00N TEXT:"launched a pressure campaign"] on Cuba that has largely blocked oil from reaching the island. The US [USN:L6N45I003 TEXT:"war on Iran"] started with US-Israeli strikes in February.
The comments stood in sharp contrast to the bonhomie on display earlier this week at the White House, where President Donald Trump [USN:L8N45G1YG TEXT:"feted"] Chinese leader Xi Jinping with military flyovers and at a lavish state dinner.
"Major countries should have special responsibilities for safeguarding international peace and security, and they should take the lead in complying with the rules, upholding rule of law, and doing what's right," Han said.
"China holds that the sovereignty and security of countries in the Middle East, including the Gulf, should be respected."
Trump [USN:S0N4310AW TEXT:"warned Xi"] against providing support to Iran during the Washington talks and received assurances that China would not do so, the US ambassador to China said on Friday.
The warning followed reports that Beijing had supplied Iran with shoulder-fired air-defense missile launchers and that Tehran had found ways to evade sanctions on its oil sales with Chinese help.
CALL FOR END OF BLOCKADE ON CUBA On Cuba, Han said: "China urges the relevant country to immediately stop using threat of force against Cuba and immediately and completely lift the blockade and sanctions against Cuba."
Cuba's electrical grid [USN:S0N44A00N TEXT:"suffered a total collapse"] earlier this month, plunging the nation into darkness and leaving millions without power as the US presses its blockade.
Cuba's aging power generation system has been under severe strain from fuel shortages and decrepit infrastructure for years, but a US-imposed oil blockade that began in January has worsened blackouts and led to frequent grid collapses.
Han also used the speech to portray China as a reliable partner on the global stage and a steadfast defender of developing nations.
"China holds that all countries, big or small, are equal members of the international community, and that world affairs should be handled by all through consultation," said Han.
items.raw_description: China's vice president said at the UN General Assembly that countries in the Gulf should be respected and urged the "relevant country" to lift its blockade on Cuba.

items.title: Trump afirma que habló con venezolana Rodríguez sobre las elecciones
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo el sábado que había hablado esta semana con la presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, sobre las elecciones.
items.body:
El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo el sábado que había hablado esta semana con la presidenta encargada de Venezuela, [USN:L6N45H102 TEXT:"Delcy Rodríguez"], sobre las elecciones.
"Así es", dijo Trump a los periodistas en la Casa Blanca. "Hablé sobre las elecciones".
Rodríguez se reunió brevemente con Trump al margen de la Asamblea General de la ONU el martes y le elogió por reanudar el diálogo con Venezuela.
El secretario de Estado estadounidense, Marco Rubio, afirmó esta semana que Trump y Rodríguez debatieron sobre la reestructuración de la deuda soberana de Venezuela, que asciende a miles de millones de dólares. Rubio también señaló que Washington presionó para que se produjeran cambios políticos.
En su discurso ante la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas, Rodríguez afirmó que se celebrarían elecciones en su país.
Rodríguez llegó al poder después de que las fuerzas estadounidenses capturaran al entonces presidente Nicolás Maduro en una redada llevada en enero.

items.title: Ukraine stun holders Italy to reach first Billie Jean King Cup final
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Ukraine's Elina Svitolina and Anhelina Kalinina swept aside twice defending champions Italy in the Billie Jean King Cup semi-finals on Saturday, sending the country to the final for the first time and setting up a showdown with Czech Republic.
items.body:
Ukraine's Elina Svitolina and Anhelina Kalinina swept aside twice [USN:L2N3V802O TEXT:"defending champions Italy"] in the Billie Jean King Cup semi-finals on Saturday, sending the country to the final for the first time and setting up a showdown with [USN:L4N45H0P9 TEXT:"Czech Republic"].
World No. 48 Kalinina laid the foundation for victory with a 6-3 6-4 win over 18-year-old Italian Tyra Caterina Grant, ranked 102 places below her.
Australian Open semi-finalist Svitolina then faced former French Open and Wimbledon runner-up Jasmine Paolini, but the 32-year-old needed little time to stamp her authority on the match, cruising to a 6-2 6-2 win to seal an unassailable 2-0 lead.
The world No. 7 broke Paolini three times in the opening set and added two more breaks in the second to complete the win in one hour and three minutes.
The victory also gave Ukraine revenge for last year's 2-1 semi-final defeat by Italy. It was achieved despite the absence of world No. 10 Marta Kostyuk, sidelined by a wrist injury.
Ukraine now face the Czech Republic, who booked their first Billie Jean King Cup final outing since 2018. Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova and Karolina Muchova secured straight-sets wins against Spain, keeping the Czechs on course for a 12th title.
Italy lifted the trophy in each of the last two years, including a 2-0 victory over record 18-times champions the United States in last year's final, to take their tally in the premier women's team competition to six titles.

items.title: US jury says Apple owes record $5.7 billion in haptic technology patent case
items.author: Blake Brittain
items.creator: Blake Brittain
items.summary: A US jury ruled that Apple owes San Diego-based Taction more than $5.7 billion for using its patented technology to power the haptic feedback in iPhones and Apple Watches. Apple said it would appeal the country's largest such verdict to date.
items.body:
A US jury ruled that Apple (AAPL.O) owes San Diego-based Taction more than $5.7 billion for using its patented technology to power the haptic feedback in iPhones and Apple Watches. Apple said it would appeal the country's largest such verdict to date.
The jury said on Friday that Apple's Taptic Engine, which creates tapping vibrations, infringed two Taction patents
"Apple's Taptic Engine is fundamentally different from Taction's technology, which Taction's own testing of Apple's products confirmed during trial," Apple said in response
"Apple does not use Taction's technology, and we will appeal," it added in a statement
"We're happy the jury found for Taction and vindicated its patent rights," said Taction attorney Lance Yang.
Taction, which uses its technology in headphones and gaming headsets, filed the lawsuit in 2021
Apple denied the allegations and said the patents were invalid
The US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit revived the case last year after a San Diego federal judge ruled in 2023 that Apple did not infringe the patents

items.title: Guardians, clinging to AL Central lead, face Michael Wacha and Royals
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Cleveland is doing its best to hold onto the American League Central lead but will face a stiff challenge on Saturday night from Kansas City's Michael Wacha, who has dominated the Guardians this season.
items.body:
Cleveland is doing its best to hold onto the American League Central lead but will face a stiff challenge on Saturday night from Kansas City's Michael Wacha, who has dominated the Guardians this season.
Wacha will look for his fourth straight victory over the Guardians, who will aim to take the series from the lowly Royals on Saturday but likely will need Tanner Bibee to fare better than he has lately.
Cleveland (84-76) blew a 7-5 lead in the eighth inning Friday, via Carter Jensen's second two-run homer of the night for Kansas City. However, the Guardians drew six of their 13 walks in the ninth, including three in a row with the bases loaded, and Angel Martinez added a two-run double en route to a 12-9 victory.
Winners in eight of its past nine games, Cleveland already has clinched a wild-card berth and owns a one-game division lead over the Chicago White Sox, who hold the tiebreaker between the teams.
"There's still work to be done," Guardians star Steven Kwan, who walked twice and scored two runs Friday, told Guardians.TV. "We got a full 162, then the playoffs; that's what it takes."
Though the Guardians are highly confident, and Kansas City (68-92) is mired in a 6-17 stretch, Wacha (9-9, 3.33 ERA) owns a tidy 1.23 ERA while winning all three of his starts vs. Cleveland this season. The only three runs he has allowed over 22 innings in those contests came via a solo homer to Kwan and a two-run shot from David Fry.
On Aug. 28 at Cleveland, Wacha, an All-Star right-hander, yielded four hits and struck out 10, without a walk, over eight innings of the Royals' 3-0 victory.
"(The Guardians) are a good club, and you have to game plan against that lineup, so I always try to be as prepared as possible when I'm facing off against them," Wacha said.
Though Wacha ranks among the major league leaders with 20 quality starts, the Royals have lost his last three outings. On Sunday at Pittsburgh, he allowed two runs over 5 2/3 innings in his team's 4-3 defeat.
Meanwhile, Bibee (6-15, 4.35 ERA) has gone 0-2 with a 3.68 ERA in three starts vs. Kansas City in 2026.
While it's been an overall disappointing season for Bibee, potentially most concerning for Cleveland's coaching staff is his 8.24 ERA over four September starts. However, the Guardians have 30 runs while winning his last three starts.
In his most recent outing last Saturday against the Athletics, the right-hander yielded six runs and a season-high 12 hits over 4 2/3 innings in his team's 12-6 win.
Budding Kansas City star Carter Jensen is 1-for-7 with three strikeouts vs. Bibee. However, Jensen hit a pair of two-run homers Friday and has 27 with 81 RBIs during his first full major league season.
Teammate Bobby Witt Jr. is 10-for-27 with three home runs against Bibee.
Meanwhile, Fry is 2-for-3 vs. Wacha this season.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Russell se impone a Verstappen y gana en Bakú; Antonelli llega quinto
items.author: Abhishek Takle
items.creator: Abhishek Takle
items.summary: George Russell se impuso al cuatro veces campeón del mundo de Red Bull, Max Verstappen, para lograr una victoria de principio a fin en el Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán del sábado con Mercedes, mientras que su compañero de equipo, Kimi Antonelli, limitó el daño a su liderato en el campeonato al terminar quinto.
items.body:
George Russell se impuso al cuatro veces campeón del mundo de Red Bull, Max Verstappen, para lograr una victoria de principio a fin en el Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán del sábado con Mercedes, mientras que su compañero de equipo, Kimi Antonelli, limitó el daño a su liderato en el campeonato al terminar quinto.
Russell cruzó la línea de meta con una ventaja de 0,196 segundos sobre el "holandés volador", que salió octavo pero cruzó la línea casi codo con codo con su rival de Mercedes después de que dos fases de coche de seguridad convirtieran lo que parecía un paseo en una lucha por la supervivencia para el británico.
El francés Isack Hadjar, a quien Red Bull le renovó el contrato a principios de esta semana y que se perdió las tres últimas carreras por una lesión en la muñeca, completó el podio en su regreso a la competición.
La victoria en el circuito urbano de Bakú fue la octava de la carrera de Russell, la tercera de la temporada y la primera desde el Gran Premio de Austria a finales de junio.
Esto le permitió recortar la diferencia en la clasificación general con respecto al líder del campeonato, el italiano Antonelli, en 15 puntos, situando la diferencia total en 66 puntos tras 15 rondas.
"Es increíble volver al escalón más alto del podio", declaró Russell. "En todas las carreras desde el receso (de verano) he ido mejorando cada vez más y vuelvo a sentirme más yo mismo".
Antonelli había salido desde la 16.ª posición tras un error poco habitual que le llevó a sufrir una caída en la sesión de clasificación del viernes.
Su actuación del sábado se alejó de la remontada que protagonizó en Monza —donde pasó del 19.º al primer puesto— y se asemejó más a una recuperación paulatina.
Charles Leclerc se hizo con el cuarto puesto para Ferrari, por delante del italiano de 20 años. Su compañero de equipo, el siete veces campeón del mundo Lewis Hamilton, quedó sexto.
El debutante de Racing Bulls, Arvid Lindblad, terminó séptimo. Esteban Ocon se hizo con el octavo puesto, por delante de su compañero de equipo Oliver Bearman, en una doble clasificación en los puntos para Haas.
Carlos Sainz completó el top 10 para Williams.

items.title: German minister calls for expedited deportation in mass border crossings
items.author: Maria Martinez
items.creator: Maria Martinez
items.summary: German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt called on Saturday for an expedited procedure to deport individuals following mass border crossings, such as the influx into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta in July.
items.body:
German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt called on Saturday for an expedited procedure to deport individuals following [USN:L1N45A0JO TEXT:"mass border crossings"], such as the influx into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta in July.
“We need a new European mechanism for handling migration crises,” Dobrindt said at the start of a meeting in Munich with European Union counterparts and EU Migration Commissioner Magnus Brunner.
Dobrindt said that exceptional situations similar to the one in Ceuta had occurred repeatedly at the EU’s external borders.
More than [USN:L1N43X0ZO TEXT:"72,000 people surged"] into Ceuta from Morocco at the end of July, although most later left. Spain estimates 12,000 migrants remain in the tiny territory, including minors.
“These waves are not caused by a humanitarian emergency, but are driven by misinformation,” said Dobrindt, calling for a fast-track procedure for repatriation when authorities determine that there is an exceptional situation that is not linked to a humanitarian emergency.
According to Dobrindt, the European border protection agency Frontex should also assist countries in such situations by deploying a rapid-response force within 24 hours.

items.title: Cal Raleigh honors Mariners announcer in final series vs. Angels
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Cal Raleigh made his way up to the press box before a recent game at T-Mobile Park, lugging a large box with him.
items.body:
Cal Raleigh made his way up to the press box before a recent game at T-Mobile Park, lugging a large box with him.
The Seattle Mariners catcher poked his head into the home radio booth, where announcer Rick Rizzs was preparing for one of the final games of his 41-year career with the franchise.
Raleigh opened the box to unveil a custom chest protector with a collage of photos of Rizzs, one with Ken Griffey Jr. and another with late broadcast partner Dave Niehaus, with the words "Holy Smokes," Rizzs' catchphrase.
Raleigh told Rizzs he plans to wear the equipment this weekend against the Los Angeles Angels in the final games of the season.
"Oh, my gosh," Rizzs said, covering his mouth.
It was one of few times Rizzs has been at a loss for words.
"After I'm done wearing it you get to keep it," Raleigh told Rizzs in a video the Mariners shared on social media.
The clip ended with Rizzs hugging Raleigh and telling him, "You're the best."
After falling one game short of their first World Series appearance last season, the Mariners had high hopes in their 50th anniversary season to send Rizzs out with a bang.
It won't happen, as the Mariners (74-86) were eliminated from playoff contention in the American League West on Thursday.
So Rizzs, 72, will call his final game Sunday afternoon. Just the thought of it makes him tear up.
"I'm a crybaby," he admitted. "I cry at Hallmark commercials."
The Angels (62-98) have won the first two games of the series and need one more victory this weekend to avoid the first 100-loss season in franchise history, which dates to 1961.
Reid Detmers pitched six scoreless innings and Christian Moore and Zach Neto homered in Friday's 7-5 victory.
"That was a good way to end it," said Detmers, who returned to the rotation this season. "There's a lot of good to look back on. And to do it against a pretty good team in their home ballpark. It's a good feeling."
Detmers finished 7-8 with a 3.36 ERA and 211 strikeouts, the first Angels left-hander to fan more than 200 since Chuck Finley in 1999.
"We talked about his journey," Angels manager Kurt Suzuki said. "Being such a good starter early in his career, having struggles and then moving to the bullpen last year. And now, becoming one of the best starters in the game. It's a credit to him and his work ethic."
Saturday's pitching matchup will feature Angels right-hander Ryan Johnson (5-9, 4.93 ERA) against Mariners rookie lefty Kade Anderson (2-2, 4.18).
Johnson is coming off an 8-0 loss to visiting Minnesota on Sunday, when he allowed three runs on seven hits over 4 2/3 innings. In his start before that, he beat the visiting Mariners 2-1 by giving up one run in six innings. Johnson is 1-1 with a 2.25 ERA in three career appearances against Seattle, with two starts.
Anderson pitched seven scoreless innings Sunday in a 2-1 victory at Colorado, when he gave up three hits with no walks and seven strikeouts. He lost 6-4 at Anaheim on Sept. 14 when he was battered for five runs on seven hits in 4 1/3 innings.
--Field Level Media

DHAKA: Bangladesh launched a nationwide measles-rubella vaccination campaign on Saturday (Sep 26), targeting 3.4 million unvaccinated and missed children, amid its worst-ever measles outbreak, which has killed more than 1,000 people and infected tens of thousands.
The month-long campaign aims to vaccinate children aged 6 months to 59 months who missed earlier immunisation efforts after authorities lowered the minimum vaccination age from the usual 9 months because of the outbreak.
The outbreak has exposed gaps in childhood immunisation and put growing pressure on health services, already grappling with a seasonal surge in dengue infections.
Bangladesh is currently experiencing the world's largest measles outbreak , according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. It has recorded 1,087 confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths, including 101 laboratory-confirmed fatalities.

Since Mar 15, authorities have reported nearly 187,000 suspected cases and 21,099 confirmed infections, with more than 165,000 people hospitalised, health ministry data showed.
Health experts attributed the crisis to disruptions in routine immunisation programmes in 2024 and 2025, when political turmoil, changes to vaccine procurement and the postponement or cancellation of vaccination campaigns left many children unprotected.
Missed vaccinations and vaccine supply disruptions left children vulnerable to infection, particularly infants under 9 months who are too young to receive routine measles immunisation, helping fuel transmission across age groups.
Since April, Bangladesh has vaccinated nearly 20 million children through emergency and follow-up campaigns. However, experts say significant immunity gaps remain, with many eligible children still unvaccinated or missed during previous drives.
They say reaching every eligible child in the latest campaign will be critical to slowing transmission and preventing future outbreaks of the highly contagious disease.
Authorities said the campaign will help close immunity gaps, reduce severe illness and deaths, and break chains of transmission across Bangladesh.

items.title: Fury afirma que combate contra Joshua está en peligro por enfrentamiento entre los promotores
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Tyson Fury dijo que el combate contra su compatriota británico Anthony Joshua, previsto para el 11 de diciembre, está en peligro debido a que Joshua y su promotor, Eddie Hearn, están intentando retirarse del encuentro entre los dos ex campeones mundiales de peso pesado.
items.body:
Tyson Fury dijo que el combate contra su compatriota británico Anthony Joshua, previsto para el 11 de diciembre, está en peligro debido a que Joshua y su promotor, Eddie Hearn, están intentando retirarse del encuentro entre los dos ex campeones mundiales de peso pesado.
El combate fue anunciado el jueves por el promotor Turki Alalshikh y la plataforma de streaming Netflix, y enfrentará a dos de los nombres más importantes de este deporte en un duelo totalmente británico por el título de peso pesado "Super" de la WBA en Cardiff.
"Anthony Joshua y Eddie Hearn están intentando retirarse de este combate. Dicen que ahora no van a pelear", afirmó Fury en un video publicado en las redes sociales a última hora del viernes.
Reuters tomó contacto con la empresa promotora de Hearn, Matchroom Boxing, para recabar comentarios.
Hearn ha señalado que tanto él como Joshua habían insistido en que el combate se celebrara en el Reino Unido, mientras que los promotores habían propuesto anteriormente organizarlo en el Madison Square Garden de Nueva York.

items.title: Fading Phillies keeping upbeat ahead of crucial contest vs. Rays
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Philadelphia Phillies have their backs against the wall with their postseason hopes in serious jeopardy.
items.body:
The Philadelphia Phillies have their backs against the wall with their postseason hopes in serious jeopardy.
The Phillies hope to snap out of their late-season funk on Saturday when they continue their home series with the Tampa Bay Rays.
Philadelphia (87-73) has lost nine of its past 14 games and has managed a total of two runs during its current three-game slide. The Phillies were blanked by the Rays 2-0 on Friday, keeping their magic number at two to clinch a wild-card berth.
"Whatever happened tonight, we're not getting (that performance) back," Philadelphia interim manager Don Mattingly said Friday. "So we've got to do better tomorrow. That's all there is to it. ... We've got to score. At this point in the year, we've taken thousands of swings, we've taken thousands of groundballs. Guys have worked all year. It's not about that. We've just got to be able to get it done now."
The Phillies certainly aren't getting any help from the Arizona Diamondbacks (86-74), who have won six straight games to close within one game of the Phillies. Both teams have two games left in the regular season. Should the teams tie, Arizona holds the tiebreaker.
"We've still got the ball in our court right now," said Philadelphia slugger Kyle Schwarber, who went 0-for-3 with a walk on Friday. "If we go out there (this weekend) and do what we need to do, we control our own future. ... I wouldn't want it any other way."
Freddy Peralta pitched 5 1/3 four-hit innings for Tampa Bay, while a quartet of relievers combined to close it out. Bryan Baker logged a 1-2-3 ninth for his 41st save as he lowered his ERA to 1.44.
"I think this is one of the best atmospheres we play in throughout the year -- and obviously a really good team, too," Baker said. "The more reps we get in that environment, I think, the better. It was really fun to get out there."
Nick Fortes homered in Friday's contest, while Jonny DeLuca knocked in the other run for the Rays, who had lost three of their previous four games. Tampa Bay (97-63) has clinched the top seed in the American League playoffs.
Griffin Jax (8-10, 3.62 ERA) will get the ball for the Rays in his final regular-season start. The right-hander has a 0.60 ERA in his past three outings and has not given up a run in either of his past two starts.
"We knew we were going to be a pretty special group and play some good baseball, but as the season kept going, we just continually played consistent ball every single night," Jax said. "Confidence grew, expectations grew, and we just kept riding that train."
Jax has appeared in three career games against Philadelphia as a reliever, but this will be his first start against the Phillies.
Philadelphia did not immediately announce a starter for Saturday's game. The team is expected to go with a bullpen game with every pitcher available, aside from Friday starter Cristopher Sanchez.
"We'll have to talk about that," Mattingly said postgame when asked about Saturday's starting pitcher. "It's kind of all hands on deck."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Brewers' Dustin May takes aim at former team in clash vs. Cards
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers will be looking for playoff-level consistency from veteran right-hander Dustin May when they face the visiting St. Louis Cardinals on Saturday.
items.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers will be looking for playoff-level consistency from veteran right-hander Dustin May when they face the visiting St. Louis Cardinals on Saturday.
May (7-9, 4.67 ERA), acquired from the Cardinals along with reliever JoJo Romero at the trade deadline, will be opposed by rookie left-hander Quinn Mathews (2-3, 3.65).
Milwaukee (101-59) recorded an 8-4 victory over St. Louis (77-83) on Friday in the opener of the three-game series. Brice Turang's two-run single keyed a four-run eighth inning.
After being held to one hit through six innings by starter Robert Gasser, Jordan Walker and Alec Burleson each homered off Bryse Wilson in a three-run seventh.
Walker's homer was his 29th of the season and his first since Sept. 1. Burleson's two-run pinch-hit blast was his 25th of the season.
The Brewers, who have won four straight National League Central titles, have earned a first-round bye and clinched home-field advantage throughout the playoffs.
"They play the game well, they play the game hard," Cardinals manager Oliver Marmol said of the Brewers after Friday's game. "They continually add pressure based on the type of players they have, so they play to their strength there. And then they've got some good arms."
May is 2-2 with a 5.61 ERA in nine starts with Milwaukee, lasting fewer than 4 1/3 innings in six of those starts.
He is 1-2 with a 7.84 ERA over his last seven starts, allowing 18 earned runs in 20 2/3 innings, including four homers.
May pitched just two innings in his last start, allowing two runs in two innings in a 36-pitch outing without a decision in a 6-4 loss at Philadelphia.
"I'm just gonna do what I'm told at this point," May said. "I don't feel like I've pitched my way into having a say in anything. I'm just going to do what they tell me."
May is 1-0 with a 2.53 ERA in two career starts against St. Louis, both when he was with the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Turang, whose three RBIs gave him 97 on the season, is hitting .368 (28-for-76) with three homers, eight doubles and 19 RBIs in 22 games in September after hitting .175 in August.
Mathews has followed up a 1-2 record with a 5.03 ERA in four starts in August by going 1-1 with a 2.55 ERA in four starts this month.
In his last start, Mathews allowed three runs on seven hits in seven innings in an efficient 96-pitch outing but did not get the decision in a 5-3 win over Washington.
Brewers third baseman Joey Ortiz left Friday's game in the eighth inning and appeared to be limping when he entered the dugout. Murphy said afterward that Ortiz has been dealing with a bruised knee and might have aggravated it.
Prior to Friday's game, the Brewers placed first baseman Andrew Vaughn on the 10-day injured list due to illness, retroactive to Tuesday. Outfielder Brandon Lockridge was recalled from Triple-A Nashville to replace Vaughn, who is hitting .306 with six homers and 43 RBIs in 104 games.
--Field Level Media

items.title: In Game 161, D-backs look to stay alive another day vs. Padres
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Snakes alive.
items.body:
Snakes alive.
The Arizona Diamondbacks, who seemingly have been on the verge of elimination from the National League wild-card hunt for a week, haven't been killed yet.
Their 11-4 road win Friday night against the San Diego Padres, teamed with Philadelphia's 2-0 loss to the Tampa Bay Rays, brought them within a game of the struggling Phillies with two games left. They'll try to keep their playoff hopes alive in San Diego on Saturday night.
Should the Phillies and Diamondbacks wind up in a tie, Arizona holds the tiebreaker.
Arizona (86-74) has won six straight games, fueled by relentless offense and just enough pitching. It's averaging eight runs per game in that span and has been especially dangerous early in games.
The Diamondbacks have scored 16 runs in the first inning of the past four games, including three on Friday night. They scored in six of the first seven innings on Friday night. Arizona could have scored in eight of nine, but San Diego center fielder Jase Bowen robbed possible homers in the eighth and ninth.
Now that the Diamondbacks have made it to Game 161 of 162 with a chance to advance, the question is who pitches? Corbin Burnes, listed as the starter prior to the series, landed on the injured list Friday with shoulder inflammation. He'd allowed nine runs over 7 1/3 innings in his previous two starts.
"It was building over the last five days when he was trying to throw a bullpen, go through a throwing program," said manager Torey Lovullo of Burnes' injury. "It just wasn't working and he couldn't figure out why."
Arizona is expected to go with a bullpen game, with Jose Cabrera (0-3, 4.33 ERA) a possibility to get bulk innings or even start. Ryne Nelson and Zac Gallen were mentioned as candidates before Friday's game but both closed out Brandon Pfaadt's third win over the Padres.
Catcher Gabriel Moreno (left hamstring) left Friday's game early but is expected to serve as the designated hitter on Saturday night.
Meanwhile, San Diego (89-71) also won despite losing. With the Chicago Cubs being swept in Boston and the Phillies' shutout loss, the Padres need just one win in the last two games to earn home-field advantage for the NL wild-card round.
San Diego manager Craig Stammen said that Friday's loss doesn't make his decisions for the rest of the weekend any more complicated.
"We have to go out and play a baseball game," he said. "Getting blown out, we were able to get some of these guys off their feet a little bit. I would anticipate getting those guys back in the lineup tomorrow."
Stammen cleared the bench when his team trailed 10-2 after six innings, giving mainstays such as Jackson Merrill, Fernando Tatis Jr. and Xander Bogaerts the final three innings off.
The Padres will turn to Walker Buehler (9-6, 4.56) on Saturday. He enjoyed one of his best outings of the year Sunday in a 7-3 win over Miami, lasting 6 2/3 innings and allowing three runs off three hits and two walks with six strikeouts.
Buehler is 7-1 with a 2.57 ERA in 16 career outings (15 starts) against Arizona, with the one loss coming on July 6. That day, he allowed seven runs on seven hits in five innings in an 8-0 loss.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Braves strive to get past Marlins on way to playoffs
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Atlanta Braves, who will visit the Miami Marlins on Saturday afternoon in the teams' next-to-last game of the regular season, are facing issues concerning their rotation.
items.body:
The Atlanta Braves, who will visit the Miami Marlins on Saturday afternoon in the teams' next-to-last game of the regular season, are facing issues concerning their rotation.
Left-hander Martin Perez (lower back inflammation) is on the injured list and likely will miss the first two rounds of the playoffs for the National League East champion Braves (93-67).
Losing Perez (9-9, 3.04 ERA) is a blow for Atlanta. Chris Sale (14-9, 2.16 ERA) is the Braves' ace, and Grant Holmes (10-6, 3.44 ERA) is set for the postseason rotation, too. The Braves also feel good about Tyler Mahle, who was acquired from the San Francisco Giants at the trade deadline last month.
Mahle went 3-9 (5.13 ERA) with the Giants but is 4-1 with a 1.99 ERA for the Braves.
After that, the Braves start to dim in the rotation, with converted reliever JR Ritchie (1-4, 4.79 ERA) likely next in line.
The Braves have had an excellent season, winning their seventh division title over the past nine years. But the lack of rotation depth -- especially with Bryce Elder (8-8, 4.11 ERA) also on the injured list -- could plague their playoff push.
However, Braves manager Walt Weiss has another view, at least publicly.
"It's business as usual," he told mlb.com. "The way things have gone this year, somebody's probably going to get a bigger opportunity and make something of it."
Meanwhile, the Marlins (79-81) are putting the finishing touches on another disappointing season. They have not made the playoffs since 2023 and were officially eliminated from playoff contention last week.
"We put our players first from a health standpoint," manager Clayton McCullough said Friday. "But, outside of that, we will try to win as many games as possible this weekend, especially at home, where we've had a successful year."
The Marlins, who are 46-33 at home this season, made news this week as shortstop Otto Lopez was named Miami's 2026 Roberto Clemente Award nominee. The award goes to the player who, as MLB.com describes it, "best represents the game of baseball through extraordinary character, community involvement, philanthropy, and positive contributions, both on and off the field."
Mookie Betts of the Dodgers won the 2025 Clemente Award.
On Saturday, the Marlins likely will face a Braves bullpen game, according to Weiss. The Braves will send left-hander Brent Suter (3-2, 3.48 ERA) to the mound first.
Suter got the win in relief his last time out, pitching a scoreless top of the 10th on Wednesday before the Braves walked off Cincinnati 3-2 in the bottom of the inning.
Suter is 2-1 with an ERA of 4.37 in 11 career appearances against the Marlins.
"The priority is getting guys appearances and also getting them their rest," Weiss said of his pitchers. "We want to maintain some momentum going into the postseason. We're trying to find a sweet spot between being rested and being ready to go (for the playoffs).
"Position-player-wise, we're just going to continue to play as usual."
Jack Ralston (0-2, 4.50 ERA) will start for Miami on Saturday. The right-hander took the loss in his last outing, allowing two runs on three hits in 1 1/3 innings in a 2-1 defeat to the Chicago Cubs on Thursday.
He has never faced the Braves.
--Field Level Media

items.title: ANÁLISIS Presidenta encargada de Venezuela vuelve de EEUU sin acuerdos ni fecha para elecciones
items.author: Marianna Parraga
items.creator: Marianna Parraga
items.summary: La presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, llegó esta semana a Nueva York para la Asamblea General de la ONU en busca de acuerdos comerciales en materia de deuda, energía y minería, para mostrar que el país, que alguna vez estuvo bajo fuertes sanciones, está otra vez abierto a los negocios tras la captura de su predecesor por parte de fuerzas estadounidenses.
items.body:
La presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, llegó esta semana a Nueva York para la Asamblea General de la ONU en busca de [USN:L6N45E138 TEXT:"acuerdos"] comerciales en materia de deuda, energía y minería, para mostrar que el país, que alguna vez estuvo bajo fuertes sanciones, está otra vez abierto a los negocios tras la captura de su predecesor por parte de fuerzas estadounidenses.
En su discurso ante la ONU, prometió que el país sudamericano miembro de la OPEP [USN:S0N3ST09E TEXT:"celebraría elecciones"] como parte de una transición hacia la "democracia plena". Se marchó con fotografías suyas junto al presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, pero no obtuvo ningún acuerdo concreto.
Fue su primera visita a Estados Unidos desde la salida del entonces presidente Nicolás Maduro tras una redada en enero. Y con ella quedó en evidencia el profundo control que Washington ejerce sobre su Gobierno y la necesidad de Venezuela de forjar nuevas alianzas para alinearse con las aspiraciones de Trump, dijeron analistas.
"Rodríguez tuvo una semana de alta exposición. Pero cuando hacemos el inventario de resultados concretos anunciados, el balance es modesto. ¿Dónde están los desembolsos?, ¿el paquete de reconstrucción?, ¿los grandes acuerdos empresariales? No se materializaron en la magnitud que habría permitido presentar Nueva York como el gran regreso financiero de Venezuela", dijo el analista basado en Washington Antonio De La Cruz.
"Al vencedor le pertenecen los despojos", dijo Trump ante la asamblea el martes, mientras Rodríguez escuchaba. Le recordó que Estados Unidos estuvo listo para usar su "poder militar sin igual".
En su discurso, Trump no mencionó a Rodríguez y tampoco se publicó la transcripción de su breve conversación con ella. Líderes de izquierda de otros países que antes apoyaban a Maduro mantuvieron distancia, mientras que venezolanos residentes en Estados Unidos protestaron frente a la ONU con pancartas que mostraban a Rodríguez con el uniforme naranja que es tradicional en muchas cárceles.
Según De La Cruz, Trump demostró que Washington está moldeando el nuevo panorama venezolano, mientras que Rodríguez se mostró como la interlocutora clave. "Pero ella carga ahora con una consecuencia adicional: tendrá que explicar cuándo votarán los venezolanos".
Durante nueve meses, Rodríguez evitó dar señales sobre la celebración de elecciones, mientras que funcionarios estadounidenses mantuvieron las expectativas a raya al afirmar que su concreción llevaría tiempo. Analistas y partidos de la oposición venezolana ahora señalan que el tiempo corre para fijar una fecha, mientras expertos estiman que se necesitarán al menos 12 meses para nombrar autoridades confiables y organizar la votación.
La Casa Blanca y los ministerios de Información y de Relaciones Exteriores de Venezuela no respondieron a las solicitudes de comentarios sobre una posible elección y los detalles de las conversaciones bilaterales.
MUCHO RUIDO, NINGÚN ACUERDO Se [USN:L1N45D0KY TEXT:"esperaba"] que las conversaciones con funcionarios estadounidenses, organismos multilaterales, gobiernos aliados y empresas energéticas y mineras dieran como resultado la firma de acuerdos, aunque fueran preliminares, dijeron fuentes antes del viaje de la delegación venezolana. Hasta el sábado, no se había anunciado ninguno.
El presidente del Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID), Ilan Goldfajn, dijo que la institución multilateral está trabajando para obtener la aprobación de un préstamo puente de 2.500 millones de dólares para Venezuela. Sin embargo, algunos miembros del consejo del BID se oponen a la concesión del préstamo, informó Reuters el martes.
Puertas adentro en la ONU, los venezolanos se encontraban prácticamente solos. La delegación cubana, otrora el aliado más cercano de la nación sudamericana, abandonó la sala cuando el discurso de Trump se centró en Cuba, mientras que Rodríguez permaneció en la sala cuando el mandatario estadounidense calificó a Maduro de "dictador fuera de la ley". Según fuentes, funcionarios de Caracas y La Habana evitaron el contacto entre sí.
Cuando Rodríguez cruzó el hemiciclo para hablar con el jefe del Gobierno español, Pedro Sánchez, él terminó torpemente una llamada telefónica antes de ponerse de pie para saludarla. Sánchez describió posteriormente el saludo como "normal".
Mientras tanto, una fuente dijo a Reuters que la delegación rusa solicitó una reunión con el canciller venezolano, Félix Plasencia, para discutir los intereses del país en proyectos petroleros en Venezuela. La solicitud se hizo mientras circulan [USN:L6N458178 TEXT:"informes"] de que ExxonMobil (XOM.N) ha mantenido negociaciones para regresar al proyecto Petromonagas, propiedad en parte de la empresa estatal rusa Roszarubezhneft.
El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de Rusia, su misión ante la ONU en Nueva York y su embajada en Caracas no respondieron de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios.
El presidente de Brasil, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, el líder izquierdista más destacado de la región, dijo a CNN que Estados Unidos trata a Rodríguez como si fuera su jefe y que, en su lugar, él convocaría elecciones.
Fuera de la sede de la ONU, más de 50 manifestantes portaron pancartas con el lema "Nueva cara, mismo régimen" y corearon que Rodríguez debería unirse a Maduro en la cárcel de Brooklyn donde se encuentra detenido a la espera de juicio.
Tras la reunión de Rodríguez con Trump, el secretario de Estado estadounidense, Marco Rubio, dijo que ambos abordaron la reestructuración de la deuda soberana de Venezuela y que Washington presionó por un cambio político, dos temas difíciles para la administración interina. "Para que este proyecto tenga éxito, debe culminar en unas elecciones libres y justas", dijo Rubio.
Mientras Rodríguez visitaba Estados Unidos, medios de comunicación informaron que a la líder de la oposición venezolana, María Corina Machado, quien podría ser una candidata fuerte en unas eventuales elecciones, se le impidió nuevamente regresar a su país desde Panamá.
Nicmer Evans, analista político y antiguo partidario del fallecido presidente izquierdista Hugo Chávez, teorizó en X que Rodríguez se había dejado "humillar doblemente" a cambio de que Trump le negara su apoyo a Machado.
"Habrá elecciones, pero cuando Estados Unidos lo considere", dijo Evans.

items.title: India's election commission orders review of voter-roll changes
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The Election Commission of India ordered a review of its voter-roll software on Saturday after a newspaper reported that its chief had been questioned by his deputies over changes to voter lists that excluded millions of voters.
items.body:
The Election Commission of India ordered a review of its voter-roll software on Saturday after a newspaper reported that its chief had been questioned by his deputies over changes to voter lists that excluded millions of voters.
Opposition parties have said the lists have been manipulated to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The Election Commission of India has said differences are normal in any institution, and that all its actions were lawful.
The Indian Express newspaper reported this week that two election commissioners had raised questions or expressed concerns to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at least 14 times in 10 months, mostly in connection with the process of updating voters' lists that began last year.
Opposition parties and the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party have [USN:L1N45H06Y TEXT:"demanded Kumar's resignation"]. The CJP said it would launch nationwide protests on October 2 if he did not quit by Saturday.
The Commission said on Saturday that a committee led by a senior election official and including an independent technology expert would examine whether the software complied with election laws and rules.
It also said local officials would visit voters flagged for discrepancies instead of routinely requiring them to appear at government offices.

items.author: CNA

Six dead after explosion destroys building in Athens

The blast - near some of Athens' most visited sites including the Acropolis and the Temple of Zeus - damaged nearby houses, shops and cars and sent rubble and broken glass as far as three blocks away.

Emergency personnel work at the site where an old building partially collapsed following an explosion, at the touristy Plaka area in central Athens, Greece, Sep 25, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Louisa Gouliamaki)

ATHENS: Six people have died, the Greek fire brigade said on Saturday (Sep 26), after a two-storey residential building in a tourist area of central Athens collapsed following an explosion which the capital's mayor said was likely linked to gas infrastructure.
Emergency crews in heavy gear and red helmets assisted by rescue dogs, cameras and sensors found the bodies of six people, fire brigade spokesman Vassilis Vathrakogiannis said in a televised briefing. They were looking for an elderly couple who lived in one apartment and four tourists who were staying in another as they removed debris from the building.
The fire brigade's crime investigation unit was also on site to identify the cause of the blast after reports of a gas smell in an area which is home to hotels and short-term rentals.
The tourists, two American couples, had been expected to check in to catch a flight from Athens airport at 3pm local time on Friday (8pm, Singapore time) but did not show up, a police source said.
Ambulances stood by on Saturday to take the bodies to the hospital for identification.
Friday's blast destroyed the building in Plaka, near some of Athens' most visited sites including the Acropolis and the Temple of Zeus, damaging nearby houses, shops and cars and sending rubble and broken glass as far as three blocks away.
The building was reduced to twisted metal, shattered tiles and concrete, strewn with household items and clothing.

items.title: 日米首脳が電話会談、米中の「同盟国」発言でやり取り　高市氏説明
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Tamiyuki Kihara

[東京 ２６日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Tamiyuki Kihara

[東京 ２６日 ロイター] - 高市早苗首相と米国のトランプ大統領が２６日夜、電話会談し、先の米中首脳会談について意見を交わした。高市氏は終了後、首相官邸で記者団の取材に応じ、米中首脳が第２次世界大戦中の「同盟関係」に言及した点について、トランプ氏と「日米がともに地域・世界の平和と安定に貢献していくことを確認した」と述べた。

電話会談は約２０分間。高市氏によると、トランプ氏から２４日に開かれた米中首脳会談の内容について詳細に説明があった。また、経済安全保障を含む経済・安全保障など、中国を巡る諸課題を中心に意見交換したという。高市氏は「日米の連携を確認した。これからもトランプ大統領と緊密に連携したい」と記者団に述べた。

一方、米ホワイトハウスは現地時間２５日、米中首脳会談に関するファクトシートを発出。その中に、米中両首脳は「米国と中国が第２次世界大戦で同盟国としてともに戦い勝利したことを振り返った」との内容を盛り込んだ。高市氏はこの点についてトランプ氏とやり取りしたか問われると、「具体的な内容は外交上のやり取りなので控える」としつつ、「私の方から、日本と米国はいまや最も信頼し合える同盟国となっているということを（トランプ氏に）申し上げた。ともに地域、そして世界の平和と安定に貢献していくということを確認した」と語った。

（鬼原民幸　編集：久保信博）

items.title: Blue Jays seek to take series from Reds, end season on positive note
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Third baseman Kazuma Okamoto has been a bright spot for the Toronto Blue Jays in their disappointing season.
items.body:
Third baseman Kazuma Okamoto has been a bright spot for the Toronto Blue Jays in their disappointing season.
He had two doubles and three RBIs on Friday night in a 6-5 victory over the visiting Cincinnati Reds (74-86) in the opener of a three-game series, with Game 2 on tap for Saturday afternoon.
Okamoto leads the Blue Jays (78-82) with 92 RBIs and has put them in a position to end their season with a series win. He also has 33 home runs in his first season in the majors after leaving Japan.
"He's been fantastic," Toronto manager John Schneider said. "He's just preparing, adjusting and showing off the hitter that he is."
The Blue Jays will start right-hander Trey Yesavage (5-5, 3.67 ERA) on Saturday in an attempt to clinch the series. He has never faced the Reds.
Cincinnati is slated to start right-hander Rhett Lowder (6-12, 6.01), who has not opposed the Blue Jays.
One of the biggest disappointments for Toronto has been the lack of hitting by Vladimir Guerrero Jr., who is in the first season of a $500 million, 14-year contract and has only nine home runs.
Before Friday's game, he took advantage of a second chance to walk back comments he made on a podcast that caused an uproar.
"The main reason I'm here is because I regret my comments I made the other day, " Guerrero said through translator Hector Lebron. "I feel from my heart that my fans, my teammates, they need an apology from me, and that's (what) I'm here for."
In an interview in Spanish with Veronica Batista of Noticias Telemicro on Wednesday, Guerrero said: "The money they gave me wasn't for what I'm going to do. It was for what I already did. They didn't pay me because I'm going to hit 40 (home runs) every year. They paid me for what I already accomplished.'
When asked in Baltimore after the Jays were eliminated from playoff contention with a 4-2 loss in the opening game of a doubleheader on Wednesday, he stood by what he had said. He apparently changed his mind about an apology on the off-day Thursday and addressed a media scrum on Friday.
The fan reaction during Friday's game was mild and mixed. Guerrero went 1-for-5 with a broken-bat RBI single, giving him 57 RBIs for the season.
The positive occurrence for the Reds on Friday came when Elly De La Cruz hit a two-run double in the third inning and stole third base on the next pitch. He became the fourth player in Reds' history to have at least 30 home runs and 30 stolen bases in the same season. The double also was his 30th.
"It's really special," De La Cruz said. "That means a great season. I know as a group this season didn't go the way we wanted it to. But it's a great season individually."
The other Cincinnati players with 30 homers and 30 steals in a season were Brandon Phillips (2007), Barry Larkin (1996), and Eric Davis (1987).
"Those are great guys. They play hard. They play the game the right way," De La Cruz, 24, said. "It's really good to join them."
"He's still really young. He's still developing. He's getting better," Reds bench coach Mike Napoli said. "He's hungry to get better. You would expect him to be that superstar. He's gotten better every single year. We expect him to get better."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Munich picked as Germany’s candidate to host Summer Games
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Munich has been chosen as Germany's city to bid to host the Summer Olympic Games in 2036, 2040 or 2044, the German Olympic Committee (DOSB) voted on Saturday, as the country launched its latest attempt to land the world's biggest multi-sport event for the first time since 1972.
items.body:
Munich has been chosen as Germany's city to bid to host the Summer Olympic Games in 2036, 2040 or 2044, the German Olympic Committee (DOSB) voted on Saturday, as the country launched its latest attempt to land the world's biggest multi-sport event for the first time since 1972.
Munich, the last German summer Games host 54 years ago, was one of originally three candidate cities for the vote, along with Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr and Berlin, but the capital pulled the plug two days before the vote following local elections last week.
"The winner is Munich," German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier said at the DOSB general assembly after being handed the envelope with the winning bid.
"If we go to the starting line as Team Germany then we have good chance to become Olympic hosts," he had earlier said.
Munich's bid, which includes use of the Olympic park built for the 1972 Games, enjoys strong local support.
It will face stiff competition, especially for 2036, with the IOC having said more than 10 cities or countries had expressed an interest, among them Indonesia, India, South Africa, Chile's Santiago as well as Doha, Saudi Arabia and Turkey.
Los Angeles will host the 2028 Olympics and Brisbane, Australia will stage the 2032 edition.
There is no date for a decision by the International Olympic Committee which has changed its bidding rules in recent years, with several stages of dialogues with interested parties resulting in one preferred candidate to be put to the vote.
The IOC usually awards the Games about seven years in advance.
Germany last hosted the Summer Olympics in 1972 in the Bavarian capital, which were marred when Palestinians from the Black September militant group took members of the Israeli Olympic team hostage. Eleven Israelis, a German policeman and five of the Palestinian gunmen died after a stand-off at the Olympic village and the nearby Fuerstenfeldbruck airfield.
Previous efforts by Germany to land Summer or Winter Games failed mostly at the first hurdle with local referendums opposing such plans over their size and cost, as was the case for Hamburg which was planning a bid for 2024. Munich had also unsuccessfully bid for the 2018 Olympics, finishing second behind Pyeongchang in South Korea.

items.title: Huracán Polo, de categoría 5, amenaza la costa de México; se prevé que toque tierra el lunes
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El huracán Polo se alejaba el sábado de la costa del Pacífico mexicano tras recuperar la máxima intensidad de categoría 5, antes de que se previera su regreso para tocar tierra en Baja California Sur el lunes, según los meteorólogos.
items.body:
El huracán Polo se alejaba el sábado de la costa del Pacífico mexicano tras recuperar la máxima intensidad de categoría 5, antes de que se previera su regreso para tocar tierra en Baja California Sur el lunes, según los meteorólogos.
Polo se encontraba el sábado por la mañana a unas 425 millas (684 kilómetros) al suroeste de la localidad turística mexicana de Cabo Corrientes, con vientos máximos sostenidos de 160 millas por hora (257 kilómetros), según el Centro Nacional de Huracanes (NHC) de Estados Unidos.
La tormenta se desplazaba hacia el noroeste a 10 millas por hora (16 kilómetros).
AccuWeather, un servicio meteorológico privado, informó que, 24 horas después de impactar en Baja California, se esperaba que el huracán tocara tierra por segunda vez en la costa continental del noroeste de México, provocando posibles inundaciones repentinas peligrosas para la vida en partes de Baja California Sur, Sinaloa, Sonora y Chihuahua.
Las fuertes lluvias y los vientos intensos del huracán a lo largo de la costa del Pacífico mexicano obligaron a realizar evacuaciones, cerrar puertos y suspender clases esta semana.
En la ciudad turística de San José del Cabo, la policía restringió el acceso a una playa el viernes debido a que el huracán generaba olas altas y condiciones de oleaje peligroso.
Es posible que se registren condiciones de huracán el lunes por la tarde desde Punta Eugenia hasta Santa Fe, en Baja California, señaló el NHC.
Se prevé que Polo deje entre 4 y 8 pulgadas de lluvia en partes de Baja California Sur, con acumulaciones máximas de 10 pulgadas, lo que podría provocar inundaciones y deslizamientos de tierra que pongan en peligro vidas humanas, indicó el NHC.
Asimismo, podría generar oleaje peligroso, corrientes de resaca e inundaciones costeras.

items.title: León al frente del mayor acto celebrado en Francia, mientras las multitudes esperan un mensaje de paz
items.author: Joshua McElwee, Elizabeth Pineau
items.creator: Joshua McElwee, Elizabeth Pineau
items.summary: Una multitud se congregaba el sábado en la Avenida de los Campos Elíseos de París, a la espera de la llegada del papa León para una misa al aire libre que se preveía que fuera el acto más importante de su visita de fin de semana a Francia.
items.body:
Una multitud se congregaba el sábado en la Avenida de los Campos Elíseos de París, a la espera de la llegada del papa León para una misa al aire libre que se preveía que fuera el acto más importante de su visita de fin de semana a Francia.
Más de 600.000 personas se inscribieron para asistir a la misa de media tarde, y las multitudes comenzaron a llegar antes del amanecer, agolpándose frente a las vallas que bordeaban el bulevar arbolado y ondeando banderas blancas y amarillas del Vaticano. En las inmediaciones, la policía cerró las calles por las que León pasaría en un papamóvil descapotable.
Geraldine Pambou, de 42 años, dijo que esperaba que León, quien este año fue reprendido por el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, por criticar la guerra contra Irán, volviera a alzar la voz en favor de la paz.
"Lo más importante es que haga hincapié en la paz mundial", afirmó. "Hay demasiadas guerras".
León está en una visita de cuatro días por tres ciudades de Francia, donde busca restaurar la reputación de la Iglesia tras los escándalos de abusos que causaron conmoción en todo el país.
El papa, que ha condenado enérgicamente la dirección que han tomado los líderes mundiales en los últimos meses, advirtió el viernes, en un discurso pronunciado en la sede parisina de la UNESCO, el organismo de la ONU para la cultura y la educación, que la ONU y otros organismos multilaterales se encontraban en crisis.
También reiteró su frecuente llamado para que el mundo reconsidere el desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial, y señaló a los líderes franceses que la IA podría crear un futuro en el que "un paraíso de máquinas" tomara el control de la Tierra.
Pierre-Marie Estienne, de 36 años, estaba entre la multitud que esperaba la misa de León en el centro de París junto a su esposa y sus cuatro hijos pequeños.
"Vivimos en una época de gran materialismo", afirmó. "Hay mucho mal a nuestro alrededor, por lo que necesitamos un mensaje de esperanza y amor".
EL PAPA VISITA A LOS CATÓLICOS RECIÉN BAUTIZADOS Francia, una nación laica en la que la separación entre Iglesia y Estado está consagrada en una ley de 1905, ha sido testigo de un descenso constante de la afiliación a la Iglesia católica desde la Segunda Guerra Mundial, lo que refleja una tendencia observada en otros países tradicionalmente católicos.
Aunque la Conferencia Episcopal Francesa señala un aumento de los bautismos de adultos —incluido un récord de 21.000 la pasada Semana Santa—, un reporte publicado por la agencia oficial de estadísticas, el INSEE, reveló que solo el 25% de los franceses de entre 18 y 49 años se identificaban como católicos, frente al 43% de una década antes.
En una visita el sábado a los católicos recién bautizados en la Universidad Católica de París, León instó a la Iglesia francesa a no mostrarse "ingenuamente optimista" respecto al reciente aumento de fieles.
"Debemos reconocer, acoger y proteger la pequeña llama que el Espíritu Santo ha encendido en la oscuridad de la noche, la diminuta semilla que se esfuerza por crecer incluso entre las espinas", afirmó.
León se desplazará más tarde este sábado a Lourdes, sede de un santuario católico. Allí se reunirá el domingo con siete víctimas francesas de abusos por parte del clero.

items.title: Monzo negocia su venta a Nubank por valoración de unos 10.000 millones de libras: Sky News
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El banco brasileño Nubank está en una fase inicial de negociaciones con el banco digital británico Monzo sobre una posible fusión que podría valorar a Monzo entre 8.000 y 10.000 millones de libras esterlinas (entre 10.600 y 13.250 millones de dólares), según informó Sky News el sábado.
items.body:
El banco brasileño Nubank (NU.N) está en una fase inicial de negociaciones con el banco digital británico Monzo sobre una posible fusión que podría valorar a Monzo entre 8.000 y 10.000 millones de libras esterlinas (entre 10.600 y 13.250 millones de dólares), según informó Sky News el sábado.
La adquisición por parte de Nubank es una de las dos opciones que el consejo de administración de Monzo está barajando actualmente, según Sky News, que cita a una fuente cercana al proceso.
La otra opción es una nueva ronda de financiamiento que se espera que valore a Monzo en más de 8.000 millones de libras, cuyos ingresos se destinarían a una expansión en Europa continental, según el informe.
Monzo se ha negado a hacer comentarios. No ha sido posible contactar con Nubank para recabar sus comentarios fuera del horario laboral habitual.
Nubank, con sede en São Paulo, cotiza en la Bolsa de Nueva York con una capitalización bursátil de unos 65.500 millones de dólares.
Monzo, con sede en Londres, obtuvo un beneficio antes de impuestos de 87,3 millones de libras esterlinas en el ejercicio cerrado a 31 de marzo, frente a los 60,5 millones del año anterior, mientras que los ingresos crecieron de 1.200 millones a 1.700 millones de libras esterlinas, según su informe anual.
El pasado mes de octubre, Monzo fue valorada en 4.500 millones de libras esterlinas en una venta de acciones de los empleados a inversores, entre los que se encontraban el fondo soberano de Singapur GIC y StepStone Group.
(1 dólar = 0,7547 libras)

items.title: Rangers determined to stay positive in rematch vs. Twins
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Texas Rangers have no time to dwell on their latest setback.
items.body:
The Texas Rangers have no time to dwell on their latest setback.
They still are tied with the Houston Astros for first place in the American League West. They still have a shot at reaching the postseason if they finish one game ahead of their in-state rivals.
Texas (79-81) will look to keep its postseason hopes alive when it squares off against the Minnesota Twins (76-84) on Saturday afternoon in Minneapolis. The Twins won the series opener 10-2, but the Rangers are determined to stay positive going forward.
"We have to," Rangers manager Skip Schumaker said. "That's the only way to do it. Two games left.
"... The important thing is to come back (Saturday) and do whatever we can to fight and to try to win that game. That's the most important game. Tough one (Friday), no doubt about it, but we have to figure out a way to keep going and stay positive and win."
Texas will need to do so without Josh Jung, who broke a bone in his hand after he was hit by a pitch Friday. Jung appeared in 104 games in a season interrupted by injuries.
Rangers right-hander Nathan Eovaldi (11-10, 4.27 ERA) is expected to take the mound on Saturday. He has 141 strikeouts in 141 1/3 innings this season and has appeared in 26 games, including 22 starts.
Eovaldi has not started a game since Aug. 7 against the Baltimore Orioles. He is searching for his first victory since July 25 against the Seattle Mariners.
In nine career starts against Minnesota, Eovaldi is 4-4 with a 4.75 ERA. This will be his first appearance against the Twins since 2024, when he allowed four runs (three earned) on six hits in seven innings and took the loss for the Rangers.
Twins right-hander Bailey Ober (7-6, 4.21) is set to make his 24th and final start of the season. He needs five more strikeouts to reach 700 for his career.
Ober is back in the rotation after serving a brief stint in the bullpen. In his last outing, he earned his first career save by pitching three scoreless innings to close out a victory over the Los Angeles Angels.
This will be Ober's sixth career start against Texas. He is 2-1 with a 5.61 ERA in his first five outings, and he has walked 14 and struck out 20 in 25 2/3 innings.
Ober has played his entire career for Minnesota. He has one year left on his contract, but he knows that change is possible during the offseason.
"I feel like there's always going to be options," Ober said. "Especially when we have eight starters. Guys like me, Joe (Ryan), Pablo (Lopez) and Dean (Kremer) will all be free agents the same year. And then you have a lot of young guys that have a lot of potential behind us.
"So there's always going to be chatter and thoughts. You never know if you're going to get moved. ... Obviously I'd love to stay here. But you never know. It's kind of up to the bigwigs up top to decide that."
-Field Level Media

BAKU, Azerbaijan, Sept 26 : George Russell closed the gap to championship-leading Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli at the top of the Formula One standings after fending off Red Bull’s Max Verstappen to complete a lights-to-flag win in Saturday’s Azerbaijan Grand Prix, with the Italian fifth.
Russell took the flag just 0.196 seconds ahead of the flying Dutchman, who had started eighth but crossed the line nearly side-by-side with his Mercedes rival, after two safety car phases turned a Saturday cruise into a fight for survival for the Briton.
Frenchman Isack Hadjar completed a double podium for Red Bull, repaying the team’s decision to give him a contract extension with third on his return to racing action.
“It’s amazing to be back on the top step of the podium,” said Russell, after closing the gap to Antonelli from 81 to 66 points in the overall standings with 15 races completed.

“Every race since the (summer) break I have gone from strength to strength and I feel more like myself again.”
RUSSELL'S FIRST WIN SINCE JUNE
Antonelli had started 16th after a rare error saw him crash out of Friday’s qualifying.
His drive on Saturday was less like his Monza charge – where he went from 19th to first – and more a slow-burn recovery.
Saturday’s win was the eighth of Russell’s career, his third of the season and first since the Austrian Grand Prix in June.
It capped a dominant weekend for the Briton and had seemed a mere formality, with the 28-year-old leading off the line and opening up a comfortable lead ahead of McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, Verstappen and Hadjar.
But all that changed on the 31st of the race’s 51 laps when a crash for Williams racer Alex Albon brought out the safety car.
Russell’s 11-second lead evaporated as the safety car bunched up the field.
Verstappen snatched second from Piastri into the first corner as the action resumed, with Russell unchallenged.
But the race was neutralised almost instantly by another safety car when Argentine Franco Colapinto locked up and ploughed into Alpine teammate Pierre Gasly, who in turn collected McLaren’s reigning champion Lando Norris.
The collision sidelined both Gasly and Norris on the spot, with the fuming Briton calling for the 23-year-old Colapinto to be banned.
Colapinto initially continued before pulling into the pits to retire. He was given a 10-second time penalty but the Argentine will have to serve it in the form of a five-place grid penalty at the next race in Malaysia as he failed to finish.
Russell had Verstappen right on his tail at the second restart.
The Mercedes driver kept the lead but was unable to shake off the chasing Red Bull, with the pair trading fastest laps.
It looked like the Dutchman, brushing the barriers as he hunted down his first win of the season, might just snatch victory on the final dash to the line but the Briton doggedly clung on.
“We had a good race, a tricky first stint on the mediums (tyres) but we got a good restart,” said Verstappen.
“Then the final lap George lost boost and I got close, but it was not enough.”
Behind them, Hadjar inherited third when Piastri locked up and took to the run-off area.
The Australian, who had started third, dropped to 14th compounding a miserable day for McLaren.
“It has been a very long six weeks since I injured myself,” said Hadjar, who missed the last three races with a wrist injury.
“It was the right time to come back, I felt strong, I took it step by step to gain the confidence,” added the 21-year-old who was also on the podium in Monaco.
Charles Leclerc was fourth for Ferrari. His seven-times world champion teammate Lewis Hamilton was sixth.
Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad, who made contact with teammate Liam Lawson and sent the New Zealander into a spin, was seventh.
Esteban Ocon took eighth ahead of teammate Oliver Bearman in a double points finish for Haas. Carlos Sainz rounded out the top 10 for Williams.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Markram hopes Australia get a respectful reception in test series
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: South Africa batter Aiden Markram admits he does not know what sort of reception the Australian team will get from the home crowds in next month’s three-match test series, but hopes it is a respectful one.
items.body:
South Africa batter Aiden Markram admits he does not know what sort of reception the Australian team will get from the home crowds in next month’s three-match test series, but hopes it is a respectful one.
The matches in Durban, Gqeberha and Cape Town are the first time the teams meet in tests in South Africa since the infamous 2018 "Sandpapergate" scandal where the tourists were guilty of trying to alter the condition of the ball in the third test at Newlands in Cape Town.
The fallout led to lengthy bans for Australia captain Steve Smith, and batters David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, and a review of the conduct of the Australian team.
The memory of the incident could add extra spice to a series that is never short of an edge, with South Africa having defeated Australia in the World Test Championship final last year.
"I’ve got no idea what it’s (fan reception) going to be like," Markram told reporters on Saturday. "Obviously, 2018 was a long time ago, and there will be fans who probably haven’t forgotten what happened.
"But there will also be quite a few who have moved on and understand that things look very different now (in the Australia team).
"We’re certainly not encouraging anything disrespectful, but you hope the crowd really gets into the game and enjoys watching good cricket."
NEW RELATIONSHIPS Markram says the proliferation of Twenty20 leagues has seen adversaries become teammates and helped develop relationships off the pitch.
"I’ve spent quite a bit of time with Mitch (Marsh) during the last IPL (Indian Premier League) and with some of the other Australian players here and there as well. That’s what franchise cricket does.
"But I think when you cross the boundary, you forget about all of that. It becomes a battle between two teams who are pushing really hard to get results and win games of cricket."
South Africa lead the current three-match one-day international series 1-0 heading into the second game in Johannesburg on Sunday.
Markram believes it is a good test for both teams ahead of the 2027 Cricket World Cup that will be co-hosted by South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe.
"You naturally want to measure your own team and understand where you are. You want to know how you can keep building and make sure you go into the next World Cup with plenty of energy," he said.

items.title: For White Sox, work remains against Rockies
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: With a spot in the American League playoffs assured but seeding still to be determined, the Chicago White Sox realize they only can concern themselves with what they can control.
items.body:
With a spot in the American League playoffs assured but seeding still to be determined, the Chicago White Sox realize they only can concern themselves with what they can control.
Wins in five of the past six games entering Saturday night's visit from the Colorado Rockies show that Chicago is surging as the regular season concludes.
Right now, that's enough.
"Just looking to keep this continuing for the next two days and roll into October," White Sox right-hander Sean Burke said.
Burke pitched 5 1/3 innings of one-run ball and Munetaka Murakami had two solo home runs among his three hits and three RBIs to spark the White Sox to a 6-1 victory against Colorado in Friday's series opener.
Chicago (83-77) remains one game behind the AL Central-leading Guardians after Cleveland's 12-9 win in Kansas City on Friday. The White Sox hold the head-to-head tiebreaker with the Guardians. One of the teams will win the division; the other will head to the AL wild-card round.
White Sox leadoff man Sam Antonacci helped keep the attack churning with a three-hit game, and fellow rookie Braden Montgomery added two hits and two runs.
Montgomery has three straight multi-hit games and four overall during a six-game hitting streak in which he is 11-for-23 (.478).
Murakami's first multi-homer game since July 26, meanwhile, gave him a club-high 35 home runs.
"Right now, being at-bat, I'm feeling great, feeling comfortable out there," Murakami said through an interpreter. "So I'm doing really good."
On the bad side, Chicago shortstop Colson Montgomery on Friday broke Mark Reynolds' single-season MLB record for strikeouts. Montgomery has 224; Reynolds had 223 with Arizona in 2009.
Colorado (57-103) managed just four hits in losing its fifth straight game. TJ Rumfield smacked a solo home run as part of a two-hit night, and Ezequiel Tovar doubled.
The Rockies, who have the worst record in the majors, will turn to left-hander Jose Quintana as he tries to play havoc on his former team's bid for a division crown.
Quintana (2-3, 5.40 ERA) has made just 10 starts in his first season with Colorado amid injuries to his right hamstring and left elbow.
"I think he would have had a good year if he would have stayed healthy," Rockies manager Warren Schaeffer said.
Quintana was a mainstay in the White Sox rotation from 2012 until he was traded in the middle of the 2017 season, going 50-54 with a 3.51 ERA in 172 appearances (169 starts).
Facing the visiting Seattle Mariners last Saturday, Quintana took a no-decision in a 5-3 win after permitting three runs and five hits in four innings. He walked one and struck out two while throwing 70 pitches in his first appearance since May 24.
Quintana is 1-2 with a 4.24 ERA in four appearances and three starts vs. the White Sox, with 19 strikeouts in 17 innings.
Right-hander Davis Martin will start for the White Sox on Saturday as he faces the Rockies for the first time.
While he remains in search of his first victory since June 10, Martin (9-7, 3.84 ERA) has pitched effectively down the stretch. He's 0-1 with an 0.89 ERA in four September starts covering 20 1/3 innings.
Martin is coming off a no-decision on Sunday against Detroit. He allowed three hits over 4 1/3 scoreless innings with two walks and a hit batter in Chicago's 8-1 win. Martin's six strikeouts were his most since July 29.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Category 5 Hurricane Polo threatens Mexico’s coast, landfall expected Monday
items.author: Leila Miller
items.creator: Leila Miller
items.summary: Hurricane Polo moved away from Mexico's Pacific coast on Saturday after it regained the highest Category 5 strength, before an expected return to make landfall in Baja California Sur on Monday, forecasters said.
items.body:
Hurricane Polo moved away from Mexico's Pacific coast on Saturday after it regained the highest Category 5 strength, before an expected return to make landfall in Baja California Sur on Monday, forecasters said.
On Saturday morning, Polo was about 425 miles south west of the Mexican resort town of Cabo Corrientes, with maximum sustained winds of 160 mph, according to the US National Hurricane Center. The storm was moving north west at 10 mph.
AccuWeather, a private forecaster, reported that 24 hours after hitting Baja California, the hurricane was expected to make a second landfall along the coast of mainland northwestern Mexico, bringing potential life-threatening flash flooding to parts of Baja California Sur, Sinaloa, Sonora and Chihuahua.
The hurricane’s heavy rain and strong winds along Mexico’s Pacific coast forced evacuations, port closures and school cancellations this week. In the resort city of San Jose del Cabo, police officers restricted access to a beach on Friday as the hurricane generated high waves and dangerous surf conditions.
Hurricane conditions are possible on Monday afternoon from Punta Eugenia to Santa Fe in Baja California, the NHC said.
Polo is expected to dump 4 to 8 inches of rain across parts of Baja California Sur, with maximum amounts of 10 inches, which could produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, the NHC said. It could also cause life-threatening surf, rip currents and coastal flooding.

items.title: Bangladesh launches measles vaccination drive amid deadly outbreak
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Bangladesh launched a nationwide measles-rubella vaccination campaign on Saturday, targeting 3.4 million unvaccinated and missed children, amid its worst-ever measles outbreak, which has killed more than 1,000 people and infected tens of thousands.
items.body:
Bangladesh launched a nationwide measles-rubella vaccination campaign on Saturday, targeting 3.4 million unvaccinated and missed children, amid its worst-ever [USN:L4N44Z0Q9 TEXT:"measles outbreak"], which has killed more than 1,000 people and infected tens of thousands.
The month-long campaign aims to vaccinate children aged 6 months to 59 months who missed earlier immunisation efforts after authorities lowered the minimum vaccination age from the usual 9 months because of the outbreak.
The outbreak has exposed gaps in childhood immunisation and put growing pressure on health services, already grappling with a seasonal surge in [USN:L4N44Y01W TEXT:"dengue"] infections.
Bangladesh is currently experiencing the world's largest measles outbreak, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. It has recorded 1,087 confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths, including 101 laboratory-confirmed fatalities.
Since March 15, authorities have reported nearly 187,000 suspected cases and 21,099 confirmed infections, with more than 165,000 people hospitalised, health ministry data showed.
Health experts attributed the crisis to disruptions in routine immunisation programmes in 2024 and 2025, when political turmoil, changes to vaccine procurement and the postponement or cancellation of vaccination campaigns left many children unprotected.
Missed vaccinations and vaccine supply disruptions left children vulnerable to infection, particularly infants under 9 months who are too young to receive routine measles immunisation, helping fuel transmission across age groups.
Since April, Bangladesh has [USN:L1N40O03M TEXT:"vaccinated"] nearly 20 million children through emergency and follow-up campaigns. However, experts say significant immunity gaps remain, with many eligible children still unvaccinated or missed during previous drives.
They say reaching every eligible child in the latest campaign will be critical to slowing transmission and preventing future outbreaks of the highly contagious disease.
Authorities said the campaign will help close immunity gaps, reduce severe illness and deaths, and break chains of transmission across Bangladesh.
